generation.explanation: A radian measures an angle by arc length. Take a circle's radius, bend it around the edge of the circle, and the angle it covers at the center is exactly 1 radian (about 57.3°). That makes the arc length s = rθ when θ is in radians. A full turn takes 2π ≈ 6.28 radius lengths, so 2π radians = 360°. The animation first wraps a radius around the circle. Then it shows about 6.28 radii going all the way around. At the end, you can drag the yellow dot or use the slider to explore any angle.
